title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: usage-based billing models in the model selector
summary: The briefing's rollout information, licensing requirements and controls are supported, with minor corrections needed. The Claude data-boundary discussion should acknowledge the published December changes; two control paths should continue to the setting, and two supporting references should be cited.

claims.claim: The USL provides a fixed-price foundation for everyday AI.
claims.quote: The USL covers everyday AI work, providing a fixed-price AI foundation for your workforce.

claims.claim: UBB covers advanced AI and frontier models beyond everyday AI included in the USL.
claims.quote: UBB is used for advanced AI and frontier models, extending beyond the everyday AI included in the USL.

claims.claim: Subscription-covered model choices already exist alongside the new UBB models.
claims.quote: Model selection is also part of the USL, with some models included with fair use, such as GPT 5.6 and Sonnet, and others included with limits, such as Opus.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL in addition to enabled billing and credits.
claims.quote: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Interactions with UBB models consume credits, introducing a cost that varies with usage.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing means charges are based on the work performed rather than a flat per-user fee. The number of credits a task consumes varies with the models used

claims.claim: The licensing model for these UBB models is consumption.
claims.quote: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go consumption is billed to a connected Azure subscription.
claims.quote: If you choose to override by using the pay-as-you-go option, the connected Azure subscription is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: A Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3) can fund credit usage.
claims.quote: Some subscriptions show an X pre-purchase credits available label. This label indicates that a Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3) is attached.

claims.claim: Existing prepaid capacity packs can fund the supported services.
claims.quote: If you purchased capacity packs, you can use them with the services in this experience.

claims.claim: Copilot Credit P3 commit units cover a one-year term.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans provide discounted commit units for eligible Copilot Credit usage during a one-year term.

claims.claim: Admins must set up a billing policy before users can use experiences requiring UBB.
claims.quote: Admins must set up a billing policy before a user can use AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in because UBB must be enabled and credits provided before use.
claims.quote: Enable UBB for users who should have access to the models. Allocate credits to users who should have access to the models.

claims.claim: Spending policies, limits and alerts are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab. Select the spending policy you want to edit.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy'. This opens the policy fly-out containing Spending limits and Alerts, and Email alert settings.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates spending-policy limits.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b

claims.claim: periodLimit sets the policy's monthly consumption limit.
claims.quote: The consumption limit for one period. A period is a UTC calendar month: consumption is counted month-to-date and resets at 00:00 UTC on the first of each month.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/resources/spendingpolicy to sources; it defines the monthly period and both limit properties.

claims.claim: perUserLimit sets the uniform per-user monthly consumption limit in the PATCH request.
claims.quote: The uniform per-user consumption limit over the same period. Required on create. Supply an unlimitedCostManagementQuantity when no per-user cap is wanted.

claims.claim: The printed spending-policy PATCH call does not configure alerts.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: Beta APIs are subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Request eligibility is configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Settings > All Settings. Select Access to usage-based billing experiences. In the fly-out pane, under Choose who can request a spending policy
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences > Choose who can request a spending policy'.

claims.claim: Configuring the access-request setting requires the Global administrator role.
claims.quote: To configure the setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you need to be assigned to the Global administrator role.

claims.claim: Access-request setting changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: Changes to this setting might take up to 24 hours to apply.

claims.claim: Choosing request eligibility does not complete UBB setup.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API to configure who may request a spending policy through this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Access to usage-based billing experiences API PowerShell request spending policy'; Copilot extensibility request settings eligibility. Read access-request guidance and Cost Management API overview search excerpt; request-processing APIs do not set request eligibility.

claims.claim: Choosing No users prevents spending-policy requests, not model visibility or use by already-enabled users.
claims.quote: No users: Users cannot request a spending policy. Instead, they'll be presented with a link to learn more about Advanced AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.claim: The Anthropic access path is Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences.
claims.quote: Copilot > Settings > View all. Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. ... under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic ... Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences

claims.claim: The Anthropic access setting requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.claim: The Anthropic provider setting governs Claude models, not GPT-6 Astra.
claims.quote: These assignments are applied at the provider level and enforced across Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API equivalent for configuring Anthropic provider access in this control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Anthropic subprocessor Graph settings API' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Anthropic'. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor and copilot-anthropic-apps; results describe admin UI and unrelated model-provider APIs, not an API for this tenant setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Claude models in Microsoft offerings are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary
claims.fix: After the current EU Data Boundary statement, add: 'The EU/EFTA/UK apps guidance says Claude models are coming into the EU Data Boundary starting in December 2026. It recommends checking the Anthropic subprocessor setting before December 9, 2026: apps-only or unset selections will become All users, while other selections, including No users, will not change.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/copilot-anthropic-apps.

claims.claim: Claude models are currently excluded from applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Microsoft Product Terms and DPA apply when Anthropic supplies Claude models as a Microsoft subprocessor.
claims.quote: Unless models are labeled "Anthropic models with Data Retention," the Microsoft Product Terms and Microsoft Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention fall under Anthropic's separate terms.
claims.quote: Anthropic acts as an independent processor and use of Anthropic models with Data Retention is subject to acceptance of Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service and Anthropic's Data Protection Addendum.

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default.
claims.quote: Anthropic models with Data Retention (such as Fable 5.0) have additional controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center and are off by default for all scenarios

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention require a separate tenant-admin opt-in.
claims.quote: No users will have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in to enable use of Anthropic models with Data Retention.

claims.claim: Fable-class models may have different or additional terms, so their terms cannot be assumed identical.
claims.quote: Certain Claude models, such as Fable 5.0 and Fable 5.1, may be made available to your organization with different or additional terms

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Identity-based spending policies govern access and spending for users or groups.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.

claims.claim: A user moving between Microsoft Entra ID groups takes on the new group's spending policy.
claims.quote: If a user moves from one Microsoft Entra ID group to another during a billing period, the new group's spending policy becomes effective for the user.

claims.claim: The user's consumption history carries forward across a spending-policy change.
claims.quote: However, the user's consumption history carries forward across the policy change.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Spending policies can set policy-level monthly limits.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: Spending policies can set per-user monthly limits.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.claim: Alerts warn at configured usage thresholds.
claims.quote: Select the administrators or stakeholders who must receive email notifications when policy usage reaches the threshold.

claims.claim: Users hitting the policy limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: A running task can complete without interruption after exceeding a per-user limit in a group spending policy.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: Requests not matching a custom request policy continue through Microsoft's credit request service for resolution in the admin center.
claims.quote: Requests that don't match a custom request policy continue through the Microsoft credit request service and can be resolved in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether requests originating in this Chat model selector will reach the documented Credit requests page.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com/copilot model selector request credits'. Read monitor-spending, USL/UBB and Copilot overview; MC1519122 promises later in-product requests but does not identify their destination.

claims.claim: Government-cloud rollout dates for this UBB Chat model-selector feature are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com/copilot models usage-based billing GCC'. Read roadmap, MC1519122, UBB overview and Claude regional exclusions; none gives government-cloud rollout dates for this feature.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn has not published per-model Copilot Credit rates for GPT-6 Astra or Claude Fable 5.1 in this Chat feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Astra Credits billing rate; Copilot Fable rate. Read USL/UBB, UBB overview, setup, billing comparison and Copilot Studio billing-rate excerpts; Studio agent rates do not establish rates for these Chat models.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: How the Chat selector presents UBB models to users without enabled UBB and credits is not established.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat model selector usage-based visibility; site:learn.microsoft.com/copilot Chat hide UBB. Read Copilot overview, discovery-setting and request-access guidance; none specifies disabled versus hidden entries for this selector.

claims.claim: Support for per-model spending limits in this Chat feature remains an open question.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com/copilot per-model limits billing'. Read spending-policy management, setup and Graph spendingPolicy reference; documented limits are policy/per-user, and model templates apply only to Cowork.

claims.claim: The comparison article describes the admin center operational view as credits-only.
claims.quote: Everything in this view is expressed in Copilot Credits, not currency.

claims.claim: The comparison article says dashboard totals and exports may be point-in-time views.
claims.quote: Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.

claims.claim: The monitoring article documents estimated cost in local currency including negotiated rates.
claims.quote: Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates.

claims.claim: Admin center estimated costs may not match the bill.
claims.quote: It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.claim: The monitoring article distinguishes point-in-time exported reports from dashboard views that continue retrieving live data.
claims.quote: Exported reports are generated as a point-in-time snapshot, while dashboard views continue to retrieve live data.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges for the linked subscription.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information for Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans (P3)

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows P3 purchase or amortized cost.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information for Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans (P3)

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management does not show consumption against prepaid capacity packs.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management doesn't show consumption against Prepaid Capacity packs.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity-pack credit usage is monitored in the Microsoft 365 or Power Platform admin center as applicable.
claims.quote: Use the Microsoft 365 admin center or Power Platform admin center, as applicable, to monitor Prepaid Capacity Pack credit usage.

claims.claim: Global administrator and Billing administrator can add, select and change billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: The setup article says AI administrator and License administrator can edit spending policies and manage limits and alerts, but cannot create policies.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: The same setup article also lists License Administrator as read-only, contradicting its earlier role guidance.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access to consumption information

claims.claim: Supported reader roles can view consumption information.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: The Auto-apply new services setting automatically includes future supported services when enabled.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies define access and limits but do not reserve or allocate credits to users or groups.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: spending policies
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Cost Management spending policies govern UBB models in Copilot Chat and Office.
claims.quote: Services managed by usage-based billing in the Microsoft admin center now include: ... Models with usage-based billing in Copilot Chat and Office
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits to sources; its services table explicitly includes UBB models in Copilot Chat and Office.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating matches the documented Copilot Credit meter.
claims.quote: UBB experiences consume Copilot Credits and require a USL for access.

claims.claim: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing discovery setting is deprecated.
claims.quote: The AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing setting is deprecated.

claims.claim: The discovery setting controls visibility, while Copilot Cost Management controls access and spending.
claims.quote: In short, this setting controls visibility, while Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending.

claims.claim: The cited Anthropic subprocessor documentation describes Claude models and their processing terms.
claims.quote: Microsoft offers Claude models from Anthropic as part of Microsoft Online Services, delivering enterprise-grade commitments and safeguards to ensure secure and responsible use of Claude models within your organization.
